question.text: Which of the following is not a dimensionless quantity?

solution.text: The power factor is defined as,<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cos</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></math> which is dimensionless, the formula of quality factor, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Q</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>R</mi></mfrac><msqrt><mfrac><mi>L</mi><mi>C</mi></mfrac></msqrt></math>, which is also dimensionless, and the permeability in free space, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>μ</mi><msub><mi>μ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mfrac></math>, but permeability in free space is defined as,  <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>μ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msub><mi>ε</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mfrac></math>, here <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>c</mi></math> is the speed of light in vacuum and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>ε</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></math> is the permittivity in free space so this having dimension.
